s1.about: R-14 S1 slice (seam plan §12, ADR 0007 D11/D12): one row per S1 topic and kind with its v1 input, the row v1 posts and what the hub makes of it (n is the spec until the S1 normalisers exist), one complete snapshot page per topic (the golden entities only: v1 page tests seed exactly those) and what it resets, a two-page snapshot bounded by range and head, the hub's identity refs before and after the identity rows, the S1 heartbeat and the two S1 calls. Generated by the hub (test/support/golden-s1.ts).
s1.h_rule: looks h = lower-case hex sha256 of the UTF-8 canonical JSON of the payload without h: object keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit at every depth, arrays in order, no whitespace, strings and numbers as JSON.stringify writes them
s1.default_look_rule: a look is default (never listed by the looks snapshot; the hub re-fetches a held one through the looks call when a complete page omits it) when avatar has no url and no deco, name is exactly {kind:"solid"}, it has no text, entrance, profile or gtf, badges is empty, flairs is empty, auto is {supporter:null, plex:false, plus_pads:[]} and valid_until is null; acct, handle, display, bot, verified, avatar.hue and h do not count

ranged.about: identity/changed pulled in two pages; held = the hub's v1_feed_pos per entity before the pull. A page resets exactly the held entities inside its (after, through] range that it does not list and whose position is <= its head; kept shows why others are left alone. Hub-side (Q1) only: v1 need not reproduce the split

reset.effect: every live ref released at the hub's clock, marked released_approx (no v1 time for an absent account), account_mirror status gone, its looks_cache row tombstoned

kept.why: position 1301 > the page head 1300: its feed row is newer than the page

refs.about: the hub's identity_refs (seam plan §12.9) before the s1 identity rows apply in id order, and after; refs_seq is the page order of POST /internal/v1/refs:page (calls.refs_page answers from after). A minted ref's id here is UUIDv7(ev_at ms, refs_seq) so a test can recompute it; the hub mints random UUIDv7s of ev_at. epoch is the hub's refs epoch, which every refs-page cursor carries (§12.7)

looks.about: POST /internal/v1/looks, hub -> v1 (signed hub-<env>-<n>); 404 while the looks switch is off

refs_page.about: POST /internal/v1/refs:page, identity -> hub (signed identity-<env>-<n>; v1 gets 403 wrong_caller): a full pass
the same rows in pages of 3: the first page
the rest, asked again at once because more was true
the next poll from the stored cursor: nothing new, the cursor stays

a cursor from an earlier refs epoch (stored before a promotion or restore bumped it): the hub can't trust its position (a lost refs_seq may be reissued), so it answers a full pass from 0 and the new epoch

link_rules.about: Camfrog links: external_id = lower(trim(login)) as SQLite computes it (trim: U+0020 only; lower: A-Z only), 1-64 code points. v1 posts camfrog[].link for camfrog[].raw (users.camfrogUsername; null: no link); the hub's check accepts each such link and quarantines every bad[].link bad_link

camfrog.name: spaces around the login are trimmed
a tab is not trimmed (SQLite trim removes U+0020 only)
a no-break space is not trimmed
letters outside A-Z keep their case (SQLite lower maps A-Z only)
64 code points fit, though they are 128 UTF-16 units
trimmed spaces do not count toward the 64
spaces only: no link (an empty login is no link, not a bad one)

bad.name: JavaScript's trim() is not SQLite's: a tab-led login
JavaScript's toLowerCase() is not SQLite's lower(): a capital outside A-Z
